verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Term by term the numerator is the paper's: L h η = 1 - 2hη², D h = 1/2 - h, d η = 1 - η² are the abbreviations of (4.1), and J₀' is expanded to its (A.7) value 2η/(1+η²) (f = (1+η²)⁻¹ = e^{-J₀}, J₀ = log(1+η²)); the denominator 8/5 and the coefficients (3/5), -h(1-8η²), (D+4d) agree exactly. Two routine recodings. (i) The equality is carried by a definition (idealAngularLag = idealAngularSource/(8/5), and RadialSchedule.idealLag likewise) rather than asserted of a separately constructed Q_s; that it really is the Q_s of the paper's scalar equation is the content of ideal_lag_equation, (1+3/5)·idealLag = idealSource, i.e. the constant particular solution at logarithmic slope l = 3/5, and of idealAngularLag_is_incoming_integral (OutgoingEntranceCone.lean:276), which writes the same quantity as ∫_{-∞}^0 e^{(8/5)t}S dt. (ii) The paper's unspecified c > 0 is the explicit c = 1, proved under 0 ≤ h ≤ 1/100 (RadialSchedule's variant: h ≤ 1/5) and |η| ≤ 1; the paper carries only 0 < h < 1/2 from (4.1) and -1 < η < 1 from (3.2), but h is small throughout Section A.5 by the ordering (A.6), and h ≤ 1/5 is exactly what makes the constant equal 1.
